name: Purple (Munsell)
lede: Purple (Munsell) is a vivid, saturated purple: the color sitting at hue 5.0P in the Munsell system, one step over from plain [[purple]].

sections.title: A system color, not a dictionary name
sections.body: This entry is not a found word but a notation: Munsell notes it 5.0P 4.0/21.9, hue 5.0P, value 4.0, chroma 21.9, among the highest chroma figures the system records for a purple [1]. The Munsell system itself dates to Albert Munsell's early-twentieth-century notation for hue, value and chroma, built to be measured rather than named [1]. Our library's only source for this particular entry is a Wikipedia summary of that notation [1]. The nearest named color on file is [[dark-violet]], 3.0 units away and more vivid still, with [[dark-orchid]] and [[iris-purple]] close behind [2]. The ISCC-NBS system classes this hue as a vivid purple [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive matches this color closely enough to count, as photographed [3]. A chroma this high is rare on an aged, varnished canvas; pigments fade and glaze darkens long before they reach this intensity [3]. That absence describes our archive, not painting as a whole [3].
